newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL interbank rates stay easy in liquid market.
newsitem.headline: KL interbank rates stay easy in liquid market.

text.p: Interbank rates were mostly steady, but under downward pressure from funds coming in from overseas, dealers said on Wednesday.
They said the market was slightly cautious due to the mild retreat of the ringgit in the last two days.
However, funds continued to flow in after the nearly two percent surge of the ringgit against dollar in the last one week.
"Dollar/ringgit movements are generally dictating the trend in the interbank money market," said the head of money dealing at a Malaysian bank.

He said most of the ringgit buyers were overseas players, who could lend only to select borrowers in the local market. They tend to shy away from finance companies and merchant banks, who are considered higher risk borrowers in Malaysia.
Not much fresh liquidity was being generated despite the sharp rise of the ringgit as Bank Negara was not active in the foreign exchange market, dealers said.
One-week money was at 7.00/10 percent against 7.10/20 previously, two-week was at 7.10/20 against 7.20/25 and one-month was steady at 7.20/25.
Three-month money was at 7.25/30 and six-month at 7.30/35, both unchanged from Tuesday.
Dealers said interbank rates were expected to ease further in the next few days.
"People are wondering if the money coming in from overseas will go into the stock market or remain in the interbank market," one dealer said.
